scope: C-002 current necessary consent, minimal profile, optional preferences, owner binding and lifecycle registration

assertions: only the accepted current notice version unlocks the production session consent guard
onboarding commits one profile revision, one completion and defaults-off preference facts; same command replay adds no revision
same-revision concurrent profile writes have one winner and one current-view conflict
same command and payload returns duplicate while a different payload returns idempotency conflict without a domain write
profile changes preserve onboarding and byte-for-byte historical result facts
preferred-name revision copies expire within 72 hours without preventing later profile updates, and the API role cannot delete C-002 facts or read identity ciphertext
platform permission observation remains separate from defaults-off notification preferences
withdrawal blocks new ordinary profile and platform-permission writes without creating a deletion result
all C-002 request schemas are closed and reject client owner fields
profile, memory and notification views exclude account, seed, epoch, ciphertext and provider fields
OpenAPI keeps every C-002 path authenticated with stable 200, 401 and 403 surfaces
stable consent, onboarding, revision and idempotency errors remain on the accepted HTTP catalog
lifecycle metadata registers export allowlists, withdrawal effects, deletion scopes and retention deadlines without claiming worker completion
missing consent blocks onboarding and current consent accept/replay uses accepted/duplicate outcomes
one command ref reused for a different operation returns idempotency conflict
onboarding without preferred name succeeds and owner injection is rejected before persistence
same-revision concurrent profile HTTP writes return one 200 and one 409 with a closed current view
granted platform permission leaves morning and evening preferences off
consent withdrawal blocks profile, notification enablement and new platform-permission writes
a second authenticated owner cannot read the first owner's preferred name or profile
SessionPrincipal is the only owner source and stale notice versions fail before persistence
preferred name is optional and protected before it reaches the store
revision conflicts project only the current client view
optional enablement is consent-gated and permission sync is an observation
AES-GCM protected bytes do not contain plaintext and decrypt only with the matching key version
tampered ciphertext, invalid key sizes and unapproved key versions fail closed
